# What should an Okanagan business automate first?

A useful first AI project usually starts with a task your team repeats: preparing an estimate, assembling a proposal, following up an enquiry or producing a weekly report. You should be able to show an example of a good result and name the person who checks it. If nobody agrees what the output should look like, clarify the process before automating it.

[Discuss your business](mailto:michael.mckerracher@gmail.com?subject=Free%20initial%20consultation)

Notes on design, marketing & AI Michael McKerracher · Coldstream, BC

Tailored proposal workflow

Practical notes from the work, by Michael McKerracher.

By Michael McKerracher · September 25, 2026

## Follow one enquiry through the business.

Take a recent customer enquiry and trace what happened. Where did it arrive? Who picked it up? What information was missing? How was an estimate prepared, and who followed up? Write down the waiting time as well as the working time. A five-minute task that sits untouched for two days may matter more than a long task that already runs well.

## Compare frequency, effort and consequence.

Make a short list of repeated tasks. For each, record how often it happens, the approximate time it takes, the inputs it needs and the consequence of a wrong result. Proposal preparation may be a good candidate because a person can review the draft. Automatic pricing or customer commitments need tighter rules and more scrutiny. Start with a task where the team can catch mistakes before they cause problems.

## Use an existing tool when it covers the job.

ChatGPT Projects can organize files and instructions around recurring work. Gemini Gems can provide tailored instructions and reference material. Claude Cowork can support tasks involving files and connected tools. Those are possible starting points, not a reason to force every process into the same platform. Check your plan, permissions and actual task before selecting a tool.

## Build the connections that are missing.

A custom workflow becomes useful when work needs to pass reliably between systems. For example, an enquiry form might create a customer record, assemble a draft proposal and put it into a review queue. Decide what happens when a field is missing or a connection fails. Someone should be able to see the problem and complete the work manually.

## Measure the first version before expanding.

Record the starting point and review a representative set of completed work. Compare preparation time, corrections and completed follow-ups. Bookings and revenue can matter too, but changes in demand, pricing and seasonality affect those numbers. Keep the measure close enough to the workflow that you can understand what improved.

## What the $900 audit gives you.

My audit includes five on-site hours spread over two to three weeks and a detailed report. We review your current process, prioritize opportunities and identify off-the-shelf options and custom-build recommendations. You can implement the recommendations yourself or discuss ongoing custom implementation and maintenance from $2,500 per month.

- [Claude Cowork](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14128542-let-claude-use-your-computer-in-cowork)
- [Gemini Gems](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15146780)

# What makes a local business website worth enquiring through?

A local business website needs to explain what you do, where you work, why someone should trust you and how to take the next step. Beautiful design helps make the business memorable. Useful information helps someone decide whether to call. The strongest brief brings those two requirements together from the beginning.

[Discuss your business](mailto:michael.mckerracher@gmail.com?subject=Free%20initial%20consultation)

Notes on design, marketing & AI Michael McKerracher · Coldstream, BC

RCCV website presentation

Practical notes from the work, by Michael McKerracher.

By Michael McKerracher · September 25, 2026

## Match the experience to the business.

An accommodation website needs to help a guest imagine the stay. The Okanagan Treehouse preview uses property imagery and distinct stories for each accommodation. A school or parish has a different task: communicate its character while making practical information easy to find. The RCCV design puts both into the same experience. A template should not decide what matters most to your customer.

## Build service pages around real questions.

For a local service business, describe the work in enough detail that someone can judge the fit. Explain the service area, typical situations, information needed for a quote and anything that affects the scope. Use photographs of real work and relevant examples. A page that only repeats a service name and city has little to help a prospective customer decide.

## Put proof beside the claim.

Show the project when discussing design. Link the case study when discussing a business result. In the Cool Runnings case study, the sales increase is attributed to the client report, with separate performance information available for context. Different evidence answers different questions: a finished design demonstrates craft; an enquiry report helps evaluate the customer journey.

## Check the complete mobile journey.

Read the page on a phone, tap the contact action and submit the form. Check that labels are visible, fields are usable and the confirmation explains what happens next. Test booking links and phone links. A prominent button is only useful if the process behind it works and someone receives the enquiry.

## Plan search and measurement before launch.

Agree the pages and their purpose before writing titles or metadata. Keep important information in readable HTML, link related pages and include canonical pages in a sitemap. Preserve valuable URLs or map redirects during a redesign. Define useful conversion events separately from general visits, then use the available data to review what people actually do.

## Bring a business brief, not just a page count.

Tell me who you need to reach, what you want them to do and what is failing on the current site. Bring your existing brand material, photographs and examples of customer questions. I scope the content, design, development and launch work together, with custom pricing based on the actual requirements.

# A practical marketing plan for an Okanagan service business

A useful marketing plan begins with a specific service, a clear audience and a next step. Decide what you want to sell more of, where you can deliver it and what makes it a good fit for that customer. That gives your website, search content and campaigns something concrete to explain.

[Discuss your business](mailto:michael.mckerracher@gmail.com?subject=Free%20initial%20consultation)

Notes on design, marketing & AI Michael McKerracher · Coldstream, BC

Cool Runnings local service website

Practical notes from the work, by Michael McKerracher.

By Michael McKerracher · September 25, 2026

## Write down why a customer chooses you.

Look at recent jobs and conversations. What prompted someone to contact you? What did they worry about? What evidence helped them decide? Use those answers to sharpen your positioning. Replace broad claims about quality with details you can show: a relevant project, a clear process, specialist experience or the way you handle a particular job.

## Make local discovery consistent.

Review the service information on your website and Google Business Profile together. Check contact details, hours, service areas and the route to an enquiry. Describe the areas you actually serve, including the practical limits. Useful local content should help a customer understand the work; publishing near-identical pages for every town does not create a better buying experience.

## Give content a role in the sale.

Choose topics from questions people ask before buying. A case study can demonstrate the finished work. A service page can explain the scope. An article can help someone prepare for an estimate. Connect each piece to the relevant service and contact route. A smaller collection of useful, maintained pages is easier to trust than a large collection of vague articles.

## Build a campaign people can act on.

For a seasonal offer or new service, agree the audience, message, destination and action. Prepare the landing page and supporting creative together so the promise stays consistent. Decide who answers enquiries and how quickly they can respond before driving more traffic to the offer. Media spend, production costs and management responsibilities should be explicit in the scope.

## Separate attention from useful demand.

Visits and impressions tell you that something was seen. Calls, qualified enquiries and completed bookings tell you more about commercial value. Review these separately, using the data you can actually collect. Compare equivalent periods and account for seasonal changes before attributing a change to a campaign.

## Choose the first piece of work.

You may need clearer positioning before a campaign, better service pages before more traffic, or stronger proposals once leads arrive. My marketing and branding work is custom-scoped around that priority. We agree the deliverables, review points, timing and cost, then decide what ongoing support is useful.

[Explore the service](https://michaelmck.site/marketing-branding/) · [More from the blog](https://michaelmck.site/blog/)
